newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African shares ended down on Monday after Wall Street jitters spread to the local market following Friday's steep 156 point fall in New York shares, dealers said.

However, a firm opening across the Atlantic on Monday calmed nerves and saw local shares bounce off their lows in late trade, though firmer gains were capped by lingering dampness in United States equities.
"The market has been hit by New York today, but really has been surprisingly firm," one dealer said.
Dealers said the underlying market mood was still positive with healthy demand from both local buyers and overseas investors.

This can be attributed to the market's current bullish phase and an interest rate outlook that is heading down rather than following the upwards trend of most other major financial centres, dealers said.
The industrials index dropped 44.0 points to 9,239.4 as the all-share index shed 16.1 points to 7,583.1.

Gold shares did well and put on 19.7 points to 1,016.3 as some buying from overseas crept gingerly into the battered market. A steadier bullion price also held up shares, but local investors were still staying away from the sector.

Volumes were a healthy 883 million rands worth of trade, but dealers said the day had been quiet as more than 50 percent of that number was made up of trade in Persetel, Foodcorp and Barlows which had mostly traded over the weekend.

Persetel ended down 25 cents to 36.00 rand in trade worth 331 million rand. The information technology firm is still riding high on the back of its planned merger with Q Data and one overnight deal alone was worth 234 million rand.
Newly-listed Afribrand shrugged off an early bout of profit-taking that saw the firm hit 264 cents to end at 286 cents, up eight cents.
The stock listed at 100 cents last week, but quickly roared higher and was further boosted when the firm issued a cautionary statement saying it was in talks on possible deals.
Dealers said that -- barring nasty surprises on Wall Street -- the market should start to tick up again soon, possibly even on Tuesday.
"This drop is going to be fairly short-lived and the trend will turn upwards again," one dealer said.
On the near-dated equity futures market contracts followed the pattern of their equity cousins in bouncing off their lows towards the end of trade.
The industrials contract was last at 8,688/95 from 8,711 as the all-share contract was at 6,750/57 from 6,760. The gold contract was at 711/15 from 701.
